findings.finding: Reference repeatedly uses int(temp / 10), which converts integer division to binary floating point. The proposed unbounded valid-octal-digit integer domain therefore admits precision errors and eventual float overflow. Domain restriction to digits0..7 alone is insufficient.
findings.source_argument: For a sufficiently large all-7 decimal integer, the true quotient has fractional.7 but binary64 spacing is at least1; rounding can precede int truncation. No reference execution was performed.
findings.fix: Before package inclusion, version exact integer division (temp // 10) or publish a conservative finite magnitude bound, validate under that exact domain, and add a discriminating arithmetic control.

findings.finding: Reference uses int(n / 2) rather than integer division. For positive integers such as2**54-1, nearest binary64 division rounds the first quotient upward across the power-of-two boundary, so the proposed arbitrary-positive-integer MSB contract is not supported by this reference.
findings.fix: Version reference integer division or publish a conservative bound such as n<=2**31-1, then validate under that domain. Do not claim the original unrestricted interface is sound.

findings.finding: All3 official assertions have expected count2. Under public=test0/private=test1:2, a constant-return-2 program passes every check; this specific degeneracy is not called out in the semantic review. Case sensitivity and variable vowel-set coverage are also untested.
findings.fix: Freeze at least one distinct-count private challenge before outcomes and use constant-answer2 as a negative control, or hold the original proposed endpoint. Do not silently replace examples after observing outcomes.
